svg.text: every call is keyed by UserId — no "current user" ambient state ✓
there is NO PlaybackService interface — the facade depends on the
concrete class. This design has no seam to swap or mock.
addToQueue / seek / stopPlayback exist on the service, not the facade.
THE SERVICE — one session per user
setShuffle / setRepeat ⇒ forwarded to the QUEUE
computeIfAbsent ⇒ exactly one session per user, race-free ✓
the CHM protects the MAP, not the SESSION. Two devices on one
account mutate the same unsynchronised queue — a real race.
missing session ⇒ silent no-op, never an exception.
THE SESSION — transport state + the clock
play(song) — position 0, PLAYING, song.play() bumps playCount
pause() — only from PLAYING · resume() — only from PAUSED
stop() — position 0, STOPPED (does not clear the queue)
seek(sec) — clamped to [0, duration], silently ignored otherwise
next() → queue.next(); null ⇒ stop() · previous() → queue.previous()
advanceTime(sec) — THE CLOCK: auto-advances at end of track
pause/resume are guarded by the current state, so double-pause is a no-op ✓
there is NO player thread. advanceTime(seconds) is called by the demo —
time is injected, which is exactly what makes this testable. Say it out loud.
THE QUEUE — where all the interesting logic lives
queue: List<Song> (final) · currentIndex: int — starts at −1
next(): Song — ONE ⇒ same song · end + ALL ⇒ wrap to 0 · else null
previous(): Song — index > 0 ⇒ back · ALL ⇒ wrap to last · else stay
setShuffle(bool) — Fisher-Yates, then swap current song to index 0
index-based, not a linked list — jumpTo(i) and "song 4 of 12" are both O(1) ✓
clear() ALSO resets shuffle to false and repeat to NONE. So playSong() —
which calls clear() — silently wipes the user's shuffle/repeat preference.
Turning shuffle OFF restores originalOrder — so any song queued WHILE
shuffled is silently dropped from the queue. A real, findable bug.
no BUFFERING / LOADING state — no network here
Song.playCount++ is a shared non-atomic long —
every listener races on it. Wants a LongAdder.
Playlist has no owner check — anyone can edit.

g.text: WHY SPLIT SESSION FROM QUEUE?
Because they answer different questions. The SESSION knows
"am I playing, and how far in" — transport. The QUEUE knows
"what comes next" — navigation.
Merge them and next() has to reason about PAUSED, shuffle and
repeat in one method. Split, each is testable on its own.
WHAT THIS CODEBASE DOES NOT HAVE
No SearchService, no catalog index, no library / follow graph,
no recommendations, no streaming or buffering, no offline
cache, no SubscriptionTier enforcement anywhere.
Song / Album / Artist / User / Genre are modelled but nothing
queries them. This problem is PLAYBACK, and only playback.
THE CONCURRENCY ANSWER, IN ONE BREATH
"Sessions are sharded by UserId in a ConcurrentHashMap, so different users never contend — that is the
right granularity. Within ONE user, PlaybackSession and PlaybackQueue are plain mutable objects with no
locking, so phone-and-laptop on the same account will corrupt currentIndex. I would synchronize on the
session object — contention is per-user and tiny — or make one device authoritative, which is what
real Spotify does with device transfer."

svg.text: ① Spotify facade → ② PlaybackService: one session per UserId via computeIfAbsent → ③ PlaybackSession (transport + the injected clock) → ④ PlaybackQueue (index + shuffle + repeat) — the queue is the interview
